title: The Former and the Latter
gist_ar: نص عن الحذف في اللغة: الاختصار بيوفّر كلمات لكن بيحمّل القارئ عبء.
text:
Two conventions govern professional prose, and neither is a rule. The first is
that repetition should be avoided; the second, that meaning should never depend
on the reader's memory. The former is taught; the latter is not, and where they
conflict the elliptical option usually wins.

Consider a paragraph that introduces two funding streams and then discusses "the
latter" three sentences later. Such a construction is economical, and it is
correct. Whether it is readable depends on something the writer cannot observe:
whether the reader, at that point, still holds both items in the same order. Many
do. Some do not, and if not, the sentence is not merely harder — it silently
reverses.

Substitution carries the same risk in a milder form. "Do so" is admirably
concise, and likewise "if so" and "the ones I mentioned"; nobody would omit them
on principle. But each substitutes a short form for an antecedent that must be
retrieved, and retrieval is where a tired reader fails. Vice versa, prose that
refuses all substitution reads as though addressed to a machine, and is
genuinely worse.

The practical test is not stylistic. Read the sentence in isolation. If it
remains unambiguous, the ellipsis was efficient. If it does not, you have not
been concise; you have transferred work, and implicitly asserted that the reader
would rather do it than read six more words. Most would not.

Redundancy, then, is not always waste. A phrase repeated once, at the point where
a reader is likely to have lost it, costs a line and buys accuracy. Writers
trained to streamline everything omit it, and are surprised to be misread by
people who were, in fact, reading carefully.

questions.q: Which of the two conventions does the writer say goes untaught?
questions.q_ar: أنهي قاعدة من الاتنين مش بتتعلّم؟
options: That meaning should not depend on the reader's memory

questions.q: What is the specific danger of 'the latter' used three sentences later?
questions.q_ar: إيه الخطر في استخدام 'الأخير' بعد تلات جمل؟
options: If the reader has lost the order, the sentence silently reverses
It is too formal for professional prose

questions.q: What is the writer's practical test for ellipsis?
options: Read the sentence in isolation and check it is still unambiguous
Ask a colleague to read it

questions.q: What does the writer conclude about redundancy?
options: It is a sign of careless writing
A phrase repeated where the reader may have lost it buys accuracy
